title: Prohibited transmissions and payment
blurb: What you may not transmit, the narrow exceptions, and why testing needs an ID but model-craft control doesn't.

T1D01.why: Communication is barred with countries whose administrations have **told the ITU** they object.
T1D01.trap: The ARRL and IARU can't ban a country.

T1D02.why: One-way **broadcasting** is prohibited. Announcements, code practice and telemetry/telecommand are allowed.

T1D03.why: Obscuring a message is allowed only for **control commands to space stations or model craft**.
T1D03.trap: Contests and "approved digital codes" are not exceptions.

T1D04.why: Music is allowed only when **incidental to retransmitting manned-spacecraft communications**.
T1D04.trap: Low power, short duration or frequency don't make music legal.

T1D05.why: You may announce ham gear for sale **if not done on a regular basis**.
T1D05.trap: Profit and ownership aren't the test; regularity is.

T1D06.why: **Any** indecent or obscene language is prohibited. No word list is needed.

T1D07.why: An auxiliary station is a **one-way link**, such as a remote repeater receiver feeding the main transmitter.
T1D07.trap: It isn't a backup radio or a second contest station.

T1D08.why: The control operator may be paid when the communication is **part of classroom instruction** at an educational institution.
T1D08.trap: Selling for an employer or gathering news for a station is paid work.

T1D09.why: Broadcast or news support is allowed only for the **immediate safety of life or protection of property**.

T1D10.why: Broadcasting is transmission **intended for reception by the general public**.
T1D10.trap: Not every transmission is broadcasting; what counts is who it is intended for.

T1D11.why: Signals that **control model craft** are exempt from identification.
T1D11.trap: Adjustments, carriers and low power must still identify.

T1D12.why: Test transmissions must still **identify the station**.
T1D12.trap: No time-of-day window or FCC notice is required.
